title: Campandgoslow and Rockgeist Framebags – John Watson
content:
Campandgoslow began as a sticker and, over the years, has evolved into a brand with an extensive list of bag-maker collaborations. The latest is North Carolina-based Rockgeist. John had a custom framebag made for his Meriwether Ponderosa and has some thoughts. Let’s check it out…

Campandgoslow Rockgeist Framebags Quick Hits

  • Full bags and Wedge bags $240 (includes shipping)
  • Half bags $220 (includes shipping)
  • Variable Velcro attachment to the top tube near your stem. This allows compatibility with your choice of top tube bag.
  • All bags without bolt-on or lace-up attachments will default to Velcro connections.
  • Drive-side main zippered compartment giving access to the entire bag
  • Cell phone/wallet pockets inside the map pocket for bags large enough.
  • If a zippered horizontal divider is not chosen, large framebags at risk for leg rub will come with a vertical divider.
  • Hydration/electronic access from both the map pocket and main compartment.
  • Drain port
  • Durable molded #10 YKK zippers
  • Spine made of black 1050D ballistic nylon
  • Made by Rockgeist in Asheville, North Carolina

Campandgoslow and Bag Makers

In 2018, Jarrod Bunk and Casey Clark began Campandgoslow with a single die-cut sticker. Eventually, Casey took over the company and developed two bar tape designs, inspired by Eastern and Western Diamondback rattlesnakes. The Genus Crotalus contains pit vipers, and Diamondback rattlesnakes are some of the most visually stunning in North America.

Speaking of stunning, these patterns found their way onto custom bags.

Casey began making bags with Swift Industries, taking its Zeitgeist and adding Campandgoslow trim. “The first bags we used the bar tape on were Swift. That’s why I got the trim in the first place. Swift’s machines couldn’t fit the bar tape, which was 1 1/8″ wide, and the machines were 1″ wide, so I got custom trim made.”

Working with Swift opened the door for the brand’s collaborative efforts. Casey continued, reminiscing about his favorite collabs, “The other bags were with Neza at What Happened Outdoors. She’s in Slovenia. She made some stem caddies and used the blemished and scraps of bar tape. So I shipped her a bunch of fabric cuts and blemished tape.”

Ordering bulk materials takes some planning. “You have to buy a BUNCH of the trim. So much trim,” Casey explained, laughing with a seriousness that only small business owners understand. And with that extra trim, he’s produced a number of other collaborations with bag makers. Other brands included Farewell in Santa Fe, Outer Shell in San Francisco, Bags by Bird in Tucson, and now Rockgeist in North Carolina.

Campandgoslow Rockgeist Framebags

To order a custom framebag, you go to the Custom Rockgeist page on the Campandgoslow website, where you can choose from several options that complement the CGS bar tape designs. “We selected fabrics that match the Campandgoslow trimmings,” Casey noted. “Working with Greg has been a dream,” he continued. Once you place the order, Rockgeist receives an email and your custom bag goes into the queue.

For those who’ve never had a custom framebag made, the quality and snug fit are superb. The bag contours to the frame’s lines and fits more stably. Rockgeist’s ability to design completely tailored bags is superb.

These bags are $240 for a full or a wedge, and the half framebag is $220. There are various options, like zip map pockets, bolt-on options, AirTag pockets, etc. To order a custom framebag, that’s not included in the library of Rockgeist templates, Greg from Rockgeist will require a Photo Fit Photo to ensure a quality fit. This entails shooting a photo, level with the frame, with a ruler attached to your bike. Rockgeist uses that photo to make a scale CAD drawing; from there, it’s cut, sewn, and shipped to you!

Dumpling Hip Pack Quick Hits

  • Seam-welded construction with Eastern Rattler, Western Rattler, Brown Trout, or Great Horned Owl trim tape
  • 6L max capacity for Big Dumpling ($175)
  • 3L max capacity for Little Dumpling ($140)
  • Hip wings/straps adjust to fit 30″ to 46″ in circumference.
  • Roll top/flap enclosure so there are no zippers to fail
  • Internal cell phone or wallet sleeve
  • Closed-cell foam & 3D mesh back and hip padding
  • 1 1/2 inch belt with side-release buckle closure
  • Tag placement may vary from the ones photographed
  • Made by Rockgeist in Asheville, North Carolina

Size large pictured…

Dumpling Hip Packs

Also restocked for this drop are the Rockgeist-made Campandgoslow Dumpling Hip Packs. Available in Little Dumpling and Big Dumpling sizes. What’s unique about these bags is that they are completely waterproof and use a roll-top closure, making them ideal for regions where zippers can get caked with dust and for those wanting a truly minimalist closure system.

Inside, a single pocket has no closure, and the side straps let you cinch it securely no matter how you load the bag. With the padded wings and thick waist belt, the bag sits comfortably during long rides and doesn’t bunch up. The CGS version has webbing throughout, making for a nice complement to the bag’s material.

The Dumpling Hip Packs are available in a number of Campandgoslow tape trim and fabric options.

Roll on over to Campandgoslow to see the Rockgeist offerings.

Many thanks to Rockgeist for the bag; it really ties the Meriwether’s build together!
